correctness.rationale: For fixed p in (0,1), N=2^n, b=p²+q², coordinate-prism E_i has independent N/2 matching pairs and exact probability b^(N/2). Pairwise E_i∩E_j has probability c^(N/4), c=p⁴+q⁴<b². Inclusion–exclusion for j directions gives (p^(2^j)+q^(2^j))^(2^(n-j)). By the published deterministic Boolean-polytope Theorem 1.1, every full-dimensional Minkowski decomposition corresponds to a coordinate Cartesian split. For smaller side k≥2, M=2^k, each J-column must be empty or a common size-a≥2 set A and has probability f=q^M+p^a q^(M-a). If p≥q, f≤p^M+q^M≤(p⁴+q⁴)^(M/4); if p<q, f≤q^(M-2)b≤(q² b)^(M/4). In both cases rho_p^4<b². At most 2^n 2^(2^(n/2)) choices multiply rho_p^N, exponentially below b^(N/2). Any deficient cube sample lies in a hyperplane containing at most 2^(n-1) cube vertices, and ≤2^(n²) hyperplanes spanned by n cube vertices suffice, giving exp(-Ω_p(N)) full-dimensional failures. Conditioned on E_i, N/2 independent collapsed Bernoulli indicators have parameter p²/b, giving the same bound. Therefore P(D_n|F_n)=n b^(N/2)(1+O_p(exp(-c_p N))), also P(D_n∩F_n). Two singleton factors and any nonsingleton product are negligible, leaving a unique unit coordinate segment times an indecomposable (n-1)-dimensional factor. Independent exact finite checker found 60879 full n=4 samples, 625 products, 577 prisms, 48 non-prism; rate inequalities checked for five rational p values and M=4..128. Finite enumeration is not the proof.
residual_risks: The deterministic coordinate-product theorem is a cited published nonstandard premise; complete primary Section 3 could not be re-read due full-text access failure, although its stated theorem matches usage.
The theorem holds for fixed p strictly between 0 and 1 and n→∞; it does not cover p=p(n), endpoints, or exact all-n decomposability probability.
The finite checker tests n=3,4 and rational sample probabilities only; analytical rate estimates establish the asymptotics.

value.rationale: The Bernoulli cube-vertex model is a canonical random 0/1-polytope. Quantifying decomposability as a rare event with its double-exponential probability, sharp dimension prefactor n and conditional unique segment factor answers a natural distributional/structural question not implied by a high-probability indecomposability slogan or deterministic decomposition alone. A precise exponentially smaller competing mechanism and an exact inclusion-exclusion formula for coordinate prisms make the result reusable for conditional structure or rare-sample analysis. This is a motivated global asymptotic invariant rather than an arbitrary small slice or textbook parameter substitution.
residual_risks: The value is restricted to fixed retention p, not a general threshold diagram in sparse regimes.
Mathematical significance relies on originality of the sharp probabilistic law; an unindexed previously stronger counting theorem would undermine originality and hence acceptance.
